decision_conditions: The development must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date hereof.Reason: To comply with Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990, as amended.

The development hereby approved shall be constructed in accordance with the approved Surface Water Drainage Strategy (V 4.0) prepared by Paloma Capital LLP and dated January 2026. Prior to first occupation of the development, written confirmation that the approved SuDS measures have been implemented as part of the development as built must be submitted to the Local Planning Authority and approved in writing. All of the approved measures must thereafter be retained for as long as the development is in existence.  Reason: To comply with Policy 31 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

The development hereby approved shall be constructed in accordance with the materials stipulated on the plans and thereafter maintained and retained unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason:  To safeguard the visual amenities of the area and to ensure compliance with Policy 28 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018

Prior to commencement of the development hereby permitted, a scheme for landscape ecological enhancements shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. This will take the form of a Landscape Environment Management Plan (LEMP).  The LEMP will provide:  1. A soft landscaping masterplan setting out the final landscaping details. These details will include the following ecological enhancements: 1.1. Plant a minimum of 2no. native trees within the grassland areas;  1.2. Seed the grassland with a species-rich 'flowering lawn' mix, and planting of native spring bulbs; and 1.3. Replace the 'living ivy green screen' with mixed native scrub or hedgerow. 2. These enhancements will be achieved through planting schemes that provide nectar, pollen and fruit resources throughout the seasons, a variety of structural diversity and larval food plants, through no less than 60% native and local species by number and diversity.  3. Substrate, provenance and numbers of all bulbs, seeds and plugs / whips / trees will be detailed, as will aftercare and ongoing management.  4. Ornamental plants will not include any genera or species on Schedule 9 of the Wildlife and Countryside Act (1981) or the LISI list and should be on the "RHS Plants for Pollinators" lists (or of documented wildlife value), to provide increased resource availability. 5. Clearly defined and allocated roles and responsibilities for delivering the plan; 6. A timetable of delivery for each habitat to be created; and 7. Landscape and habitat creation methodology. Work shall be undertaken in accordance with the approved scheme and thereafter retained in perpetuity. Reason: To enhance the biodiversity value of the land in accordance with Policy 26 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

The development hereby approved shall be constructed in accordance with the scheme for nesting features as stipulated within the submitted Ecological Impact Assessment (SWECO, 26 August 2026). The nesting features include: 1. 2no. Woodstone nest boxes with a 32 mm oval hole; and 2. 1no. WoodStone starling nest box. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details and thereafter retained in perpetuity. Reason: To enhance and protect the biodiversity value of the land in accordance with Policy 26 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Prior to occupation of the development hereby permitted, a Statement of Conformity shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Statement of Conformity will be signed by a Suitably Qualified Ecologist (SQE) and include evidence in the form of full details on: a) Post creation photographs of each new habitat created under Condition for the Landscape Environment Management Plan (LEMP).b) Post installation photographs of each nesting feature.This condition is to certify that the design for each new habitat and Nesting Feature are in accordance with the approved scheme. Reason: To enhance the biodiversity value of the land in accordance with Policy 26 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.
